subject: Pass a parameter to init function

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Pass a parameter to init function
parts:
Hello all,

Is it possible to pass a parameter to a custom 'init' function in Stan (I am using RStan)? It would be useful for a bit of work I am currently doing, where different data sets have distinct parameter dimensions.

For the avoidance of doubt, I would like to create something like:

fExampleInit <- function(aLenParam){
list(beta=array(rnorm(aLenParam), dim=c(aLenParam)))
}

Then pass this to:

fit <- stan('aModel.stan',init=fExampleInit,data=data)

Best,

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Pass a parameter to init function
parts:
On Thursday, March 17, 2016 at 10:57:04 PM UTC-4, Ben Lambert wrote:
Is it possible to pass a parameter to a custom 'init' function in Stan (I am using RStan)? It would be useful for a bit of work I am currently doing, where different data sets have distinct parameter dimensions.

No. The only argument passed to the init function is the chain_id.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pass a parameter to init function
parts:
Although it's not technically passing an arg to the init
function, you can do it implicitly by having vaiables in the
but you do get scoping out of definitions in R, so you can
have an init function

> f <- function(c) list(rho=runif(K,-1,1))

which won't even run out of the box

> f(2)
Error in runif(K, -1, 1) : object 'K' not found

and then set the variable in it (can't do that in C++)!

> K <- 3

and then eval to get rho to be a 3-vector

> f(2)
$rho
[1] 0.9084397 0.8430041 0.4831463

and then change K:

> K <- 4

and eval again:

> f(2)
$rho
[1] -0.79284105 -0.14985411 -0.05549911 0.65483971

So as long as you can get in and set the parameter, the init
function f can depend on it.

- Bob
